messages.content: Write a short scene in modern American English between Tiffany and Maya while they are walking home from school. Keep each character's knowledge limited to what has actually been established in the scene. They know each other well and both know Tony, but they do not know about any future danger, kidnapping, hidden tracker, secret plans, or events that have not happened. Do not give either character unexplained knowledge or suspicious feelings about events that have not occurred. Keep the conversation ordinary and natural.

“I still can't believe you volunteered for that.”

Maya looked over at Tiffany. “I didn't volunteer. I was chosen.”

“You raised your hand.”

“I raised my hand because everyone else was pretending not to hear the question.”

“That is literally volunteering.”

Maya sighed. “Fine. Technically.”

Tiffany laughed and stepped around a patch of grass pushing through a crack in the sidewalk.

“You'll be fine,” she said.

“You always say that.”

“Because you're always convinced something terrible is about to happen.”

“I prefer the term prepared.”

“You brought three pens to English.”

“Exactly.”

“You only needed one.”

“You never know.”

Tiffany shook her head. “You're impossible.”

Maya smiled. “And yet here you are.”

“Unfortunately, I've known you too long to escape now.”

They kept walking, talking about homework and what they might eat later. Nothing about the afternoon felt unusual. It was just another walk home, another stretch of sidewalk, another conversation neither of them would think much about tomorrow.”
